name: Classify-and-Count phenotype distribution over a quasi-random genotype probe
source: Kouvaris et al. 2017, PLOS Comput Biol 13(4):e1005358; Methods 'Estimating the empirical distributions'; code findErrors.m
mathematical_definition: Empirical push-forward measure. For fixed developmental map B, P_hat(s) = (1/n) * sum_k 1[ classify(develop(G_k, B)) == s ], where {G_k} are n points in [-1,1]^N and classify() bins an adult phenotype by sign into a discrete pattern.
sampling_protocol: n = 5000 (5e5 for the entropy variant). Points are a scrambled Sobol low-discrepancy sequence: sobolset(N,'Skip',500,'Leap',0) with Matousek affine-Owen scramble, mapped to [-1,1]. CRITICAL: the probe set is drawn ONCE and reused at every time point and in every arm.
computational_cost: n developmental simulations of T steps on an N-node network per estimate. For N=16, T=10, n=5000 this is ~8e5 node updates, i.e. milliseconds. Cost was never the constraint on running this detector longitudinally.
what_it_detects: Whether the evolved map's expressible-phenotype distribution has concentrated on the selected targets (canalisation), spread over the structural family (generalisation), or stayed diffuse (under-fitting).
what_it_cannot_detect: Anything about the current organism's one-step adjacent possible; anything about the variation operator, which never enters the estimate; any uncertainty, because it was run without replication.
transferable_to_SFE: YES, and the transferable piece is the PROTOCOL not the statistic: draw the probe once, freeze it, reuse it across every checkpoint and every arm. That converts between-arm and between-time differences into same-probe contrasts for free. Directly applicable to HC-T01, whose frozen config specifies sample count but not shared draws.

name: Constructed environment class with a held-out subset
source: Kouvaris et al. 2017, PLOS Comput Biol 13(4):e1005358; S1 Appendix 'Varying Selective Environments'
mathematical_definition: A class C of target phenotypes generated by k independent binary modules of equal size, giving 2^k members (here k=4, N=16, 8 retained after discarding bitwise complements). A training subset T subset C with |T| < |C| is selected for; C \ T is never selected for and constitutes the test set.
sampling_protocol: Training set fixed at 3 patterns, given explicitly in S1 eq.(2). Sensitivity checked by exhaustive enumeration of all 2^16 subsets, using Hebb's rule in place of evolution for tractability.
computational_cost: negligible; it is a construction, not a measurement.
what_it_detects: Separates 'the system reproduces what it was selected for' from 'the system produces unselected members of the same structural family'. Without it, generalisation cannot be defined non-circularly.
what_it_cannot_detect: Generalisation outside the constructed class. The class defines the regularity, so the experiment can only test induction over a regularity the experimenter built.
transferable_to_SFE: YES and it is the cheapest upgrade available to HC-T01, which currently has a single fixed target and therefore cannot separate ACQUIRES_FASTER from REACHES_PREVIOUSLY_UNREACHABLE. A second period-5 target never selected for would supply it.

name: Chi-squared lack of fit against a distribution generated by an IDEAL map
source: Kouvaris et al. 2017, PLOS Comput Biol 13(4):e1005358; Methods 'Chi-squared error'; code findErrors.m
mathematical_definition: chi2 = sum_i (O(s_i) - E(s_i))^2 / E(s_i) over discrete phenotype categories.
sampling_protocol: NOT documented in the paper and recovered only from code: the expected distribution E is produced by developing the SAME probe set H through an ideal Hebbian matrix, Ideal_B = Hebbian(Training_Set, lr=2) for training error and Hebbian(Test_Set, lr=2) for test error. E is therefore not a uniform distribution over targets.
computational_cost: one extra pass of the probe set per reference distribution; negligible.
what_it_detects: Distance between the realised and an idealised variational structure, on one scale.
what_it_cannot_detect: Direction of the mismatch, and which phenotypes are missing. The scalar hides the identity of the unreached members, which is exactly the information the acquisition assay later needs.
transferable_to_SFE: PARTIAL, and with a warning. Referencing against an 'ideal' constructed by a learning rule embeds a theory of what the right answer is. Prometheus should prefer a reference that does not presuppose the mechanism under test, or report both.
verified_from: findErrors.m (Hebbian ideal, undocumented in the paper)

name: Shannon entropy of the induced phenotype distribution, with a known attainable range
source: Kouvaris et al. 2017, PLOS Comput Biol 13(4):e1005358; S1 Appendix Fig D (ADDED at publication; absent from the preprint)
mathematical_definition: H = -sum_i P(s_i) log2 P(s_i) over the discrete phenotype categories.
what_it_detects: Degree of canalisation on an absolute, interpretable scale. For k independent binary modules the generalising optimum is EXACTLY k bits (here 4); over-fitting reads below k; the untrained map reads N bits (here 16).
what_it_cannot_detect: WHICH phenotypes are retained. Two maps with identical entropy can cover disjoint parts of the class.
transferable_to_SFE: YES, and this is the single best statistic in the paper. It has a PREDICTED value derived from the problem structure before the run (k bits), so it is a gate with a computable attainable range rather than a threshold chosen after seeing data. That property is what Prometheus's own gate doctrine demands and it is rare in this literature.
verified_from: absence verified in the preprint text

name: Freeze the map, re-randomise the genotype, count generations to target
source: Kouvaris et al. 2017, PLOS Comput Biol 13(4):e1005358 Fig 5; inherited from Parter, Kashtan & Alon 2008 (ref [34])
mathematical_definition: For each target s and each evolved map B: median over R runs of min{ t : fitness(develop(G_t, B), s) == max }, with runs that never attain the target censored at the budget.
sampling_protocol: R = 1000 independent runs per target per arm; budget 2500 generations; G re-initialised uniformly at random; B held fixed.
computational_cost: R * budget developmental simulations per cell; the most expensive part of the paper and still trivial by modern standards.
what_it_detects: Three distinguishable outcomes rather than one: GENERALISES_IMMEDIATELY (already expressed), ACQUIRES_FASTER (lower median), REACHES_PREVIOUSLY_UNREACHABLE (censored under one arm and not another).
what_it_cannot_detect: Anything within-run. It is an endpoint assay by construction; it says nothing about when during evolution the capacity appeared.
transferable_to_SFE: YES, and the censoring convention is the transferable detail. Reporting the count of runs that never attain the target, separately from the median time of those that do, is what lets the three outcome types be distinguished. HC-T01's current acquisition metric (best_fitness) cannot do this.
verified_from: article XML Results and Fig 5 caption

name: One-step mutational-effect distribution and M-matrix, population-wide, shared draws
source: recovered code KKouvaris/Phenotypic-Plasticity-Logical-Inference: computeM.m, evalMutCorr.m. UNREPORTED: appears in no publication and zero times in 159 thesis pages.
mathematical_definition: For each individual i and each of m single mutations j: d_ij = phenotype(mutant_ij) - phenotype(parent_i). The mutational variance is mean(var(d)) and the mutational correlation matrix is corr over trait pairs of d, averaged over individuals.
sampling_protocol: m = 300 single mutations per individual, applied to every individual in the population. Structural change with probability alpha = 0.2, else a weight perturbation N(0, 0.5). CRITICAL: the mutation draws rand_a and rand_m are generated once, saved to rand_nums.mat, and REUSED ACROSS REPLICATES. Unstable developmental states are filtered out.
computational_cost: m * population_size developmental simulations per measurement; linear and cheap.
what_it_detects: The actual one-variation-step offspring cloud, per individual, and its covariance structure. This is the A-local object HC-T01 proposes to measure.
what_it_cannot_detect: As implemented: any trajectory. It loads one saved population per replicate and has no loop over generations, so it is endpoint-only.
transferable_to_SFE: YES, and this is the most directly reusable object found in the pass. It is a working, population-wide, same-probe local detector. Making it longitudinal is a loop, not a research problem. Its existence is also the evidence that the missing composition is a reporting choice rather than a capability gap.
verified_from: zero-hit term census over the thesis text

name: Fraction of offspring fitter than the parent, sampled with the ACTUAL evolutionary operator
source: Petak et al. 2025, PNAS, PMC12745803 (descendant; verified from Europe PMC full text)
mathematical_definition: p(t) = fraction of sampled offspring of the current best genotype whose fitness exceeds the parent's, evaluated under the current and the next target.
sampling_protocol: Offspring generated with, quoting the paper, 'the same mutation operation used in the evolutionary runs'; 2,500 clones for robustness, 10,000 for phenotypic variability; measured after each environmental change; 15 replicates with 95% confidence intervals.
computational_cost: thousands of developmental evaluations per checkpoint; cheap.
what_it_detects: Whether the local offspring cloud is becoming enriched for phenotypes that will be adaptive after the NEXT environmental switch.
what_it_cannot_detect: Which mechanism produced the enrichment; the intervention in that paper is selection-side.
transferable_to_SFE: YES and it should be adopted rather than re-derived. It is the published state of the art for a local longitudinal accessibility statistic and it arrives with a replication and interval convention already fixed.
verified_from: Europe PMC full-text XML of PMC12745803
